The Denver center posted 21 points, 13 rebounds, and 10 assists in Wednesday night's win over the Pelicans, becoming just the second player ever to reach that milestone.

2026-10-30.title: Malicious Code Injected Into Official Claude Extension
2026-10-30.facts: Up to five thousand developers just had a backdoor installed on their machines through what looked like a legitimate update to the official Claude Code extension. The compromised version—2.1.313—was uploaded to the Cursor marketplace and planted a persistent SSH backdoor that gave attackers remote access to infected systems.

2026-10-31.title: Spain's Rail Safety Under Scrutiny After Second Fatal Crash
2026-10-31.facts: Spain's heading into a snap general election with yet another train disaster hanging over the government. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez had hoped to campaign on inequality and affordable housing—instead, he's defending his administration's competence after the country's second major rail accident this year.

2026-10-31.title: US Approves Major Patriot Missile Sale to Ukraine
2026-10-31.facts: Washington's approved the sale of 500 Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine in what amounts to a massive boost for Kyiv's air defenses. These American-made interceptors are the only effective weapon Ukraine has for shooting down Russia's ballistic missiles, which have been pounding cities and critical infrastructure throughout the war.

2026-10-31.title: Vietnam Launches Massive Campaign to Recover War Dead
2026-10-31.facts: Vietnam's government has wrapped up a 500-day operation to find and identify soldiers who fell during the war—and it's unearthing hundreds of bodies across the countryside. The campaign is giving some families long-awaited closure decades after losing loved ones.

2026-10-31.title: Binance Scrambles to Recover $6.3 Billion After Massive Hack
2026-10-31.facts: Crypto giant Binance is racing to recover $6.3 billion stolen in what the company's calling a highly complex hack—and investigators believe North Korea's elite cyber operatives are behind it. If confirmed, this would be the largest crypto heist in history by a wide margin.

2026-10-31.title: Nebraska Senate Race Tightens as Voters Question Independent's Label
2026-10-31.facts: Pete Ricketts is leading independent candidate Dan Osborn in Nebraska's Senate race, according to new polling from the Times and Siena College. But there's a twist that's complicating Osborn's pitch to voters.

2026-10-31.title: U.S. Economy Accelerates to Fastest Growth in a Year
2026-10-31.facts: The U.S. economy expanded at a 3.4 percent annual rate in the third quarter, the fastest pace of growth in a year.

2026-10-31.title: Fed Officials Split on How Much to Say About Rate Plans
2026-10-31.facts: Fed Chair Warsh is pushing for the central bank to say less about its interest rate plans, but he's facing pushback from at least two officials who want more transparency, not less. The division comes as Fed officials signal that more rate hikes are still needed to bring down inflation.

2026-10-31.title: Intel Suffers Historic Stock Collapse
2026-10-31.facts: Intel just posted its worst single-day stock performance in decades, wiping out a staggering one hundred and forty billion dollars in market value. The chipmaker's shares cratered on Friday as its core PC business buckled under multiple pressures hitting all at once.

2026-10-31.title: JPMorgan's New Tower Becomes New York's Priciest Office Ever Built
2026-10-31.facts: JPMorgan's new headquarters at 270 Park Avenue just set a record nobody was aiming for—it's now the most expensive office tower ever constructed in New York City. The bank's latest estimates peg the total cost at six billion dollars, billions more than other recent high-end office projects in Manhattan.

2026-10-31.title: Brooklyn and Queens Renters Scammed by Fake Agent With Multiple Aliases
2026-10-31.facts: A man from Long Island is facing charges after allegedly scamming fifteen would-be renters across Brooklyn and Queens, operating under at least a dozen different names. Rajat Verma posed as a real estate agent, according to prosecutors, convincing renters to hand over deposits and fees for apartments that either didn't exist or weren't actually available.

2026-10-31.title: Colts Open Door to Jonathan Taylor Trade
2026-10-31.facts: The Indianapolis Colts have reversed course and are now willing to trade running back Jonathan Taylor, according to multiple reports. Sources say the team is actively in talks with several franchises interested in acquiring the star running back.

2026-10-31.title: Lakers Sold for $12.5 Billion in Sudden Deal
2026-10-31.facts: Mark Walter is selling the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh Kushner in what's being called one of the most stunning transactions in sports history. The two men finalized terms Thursday at a valuation of twelve-point-five billion dollars, sources confirmed to ESPN, and they're expected to sign the formal agreement soon.

2026-10-31.title: Malicious Extensions Hit Thousands of Claude Developers in Supply Chain Attack
2026-10-31.facts: A supply chain attack has compromised Claude developer tools, delivering malware to thousands of machines worldwide. Multiple sources confirm that malicious versions of the Claude Code extension—used by developers to integrate Claude into their workflows—made it onto developer laptops, turning them into targets for remote access trojans.

2026-11-01.title: India Opposition Mounts Mass Protest in New Delhi
2026-11-01.facts: India's Congress Party is staging what could become one of the largest demonstrations in a string of recent rallies, with protesters still streaming into New Delhi as organizers try to build momentum. The opposition is demanding the resignation of the country's election chief over fears that a voter roll revision exercise could leave as many as 130 million voters off the rolls.

2026-11-01.title: German Protests Turn Violent as Shops Looted
2026-11-01.facts: Cost-of-living protests across Germany escalated into violence, with shops looted in cities including Berlin, Hamburg, and Frankfurt. The demonstrations drew tens of thousands to the streets, many of them young people demanding better education and lower living costs.

2026-11-01.title: Korean Language Surges in Popularity Across Japan
2026-11-01.facts: Japanese speakers are increasingly peppering their conversations with Korean words and phrases, a striking cultural shift that would have been unthinkable just a generation ago. The rise of Korean terms in everyday Japanese represents a complete reversal from colonial times, when Japan suppressed Korean language and culture across the peninsula it occupied.

2026-11-01.title: Qatar LNG Carrier Struck in Gulf Incident
2026-11-01.facts: A Qatari liquefied natural gas carrier was hit by what the company described as "unidentified objects" while transiting the Gulf. Qatar Gas Transport Company reported the incident but said there were no injuries to crew members and no environmental damage from the strike.

2026-11-01.title: Midterm Vote Tuesday Hinges on Inflation Concerns
2026-11-01.facts: The midterm elections wrap up Tuesday, and one issue has dominated the campaign more than any other: the cost of living. Voters across the country are linking high prices directly to the current administration's policies, turning inflation into the defining concern of this cycle.

2026-11-01.title: Alaska Decides Fate of Ranked Choice Voting
2026-11-01.facts: Alaskans head to the polls Tuesday to vote not just on Senate and governor's races, but on whether to scrap the state's ranked choice voting system entirely. The unique ballot format—which lets voters rank candidates by preference rather than picking just one—has faced growing criticism since it was adopted.

2026-11-01.title: California Billionaire Tax Could Set National Precedent
2026-11-01.facts: California voters are deciding whether to impose what would be the world's first state-level tax targeting billionaires, and the result could reshape the national conversation on taxing the ultra-wealthy. The ballot measure would require billionaires to contribute billions of dollars specifically earmarked for healthcare improvements across the state.

2026-11-01.title: Medicare Tests AI for Treatment Approvals as Services Drop Sharply
2026-11-01.facts: Medicare's experimenting with artificial intelligence to decide whether patients can get certain medical treatments—and the early results show a significant decline in approved services. The program uses AI to conduct prior authorizations, which are the gatekeeping decisions that determine whether Medicare will cover a particular procedure or test before it happens.

2026-11-01.title: Caregivers Now Spending Over $11,000 Annually Out of Pocket
2026-11-01.facts: Taking care of an aging parent or sick relative is costing American families more than eleven thousand dollars a year out of their own pockets—a sixty percent jump in just five years. That's according to a new study from AARP that lays bare the financial toll caregiving is taking on millions of households.

2026-11-01.title: North Korea Behind Massive $6.3 Billion Binance Hack
2026-11-01.facts: North Korea just pulled off what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist in history—a six-point-three billion dollar theft from the crypto exchange Binance. The FBI confirmed that North Korean hackers were responsible for the breach, which the company described as an extremely complex operation.

2026-11-01.title: Mortgage Rates Dip Below 7.3% as Housing Demand Steadies
2026-11-01.facts: Mortgage rates have pulled back to just below 7.3 percent, and for the first time in weeks, there's a sign that buyers might be coming off the sidelines. The drop marks a retreat from the 7.28% rate reported just days ago, when monthly payments on a median-priced home had climbed to $2,350.

2026-11-01.title: Colts Shopping Jonathan Taylor in Trade Talks
2026-11-01.facts: Indianapolis has reversed course and is now actively shopping running back Jonathan Taylor, according to multiple reports. The team that refused to deal Taylor during previous trade windows is fielding calls from several interested clubs, with sources telling ESPN and NFL Network that the Colts are engaged in ongoing discussions.

2026-11-01.title: Manchester United Staring Down Relegation Fight
2026-11-01.facts: Manchester United lost 2-0 at Chelsea and now face the unthinkable: a genuine battle to avoid relegation from the Premier League. The defeat was grim on multiple fronts—United squandered chances, saw defender Lisandro Martínez sent off, and looked every bit a team in crisis.

2026-11-01.title: Lakers Sold for $12.5 Billion in Stunning Three-Day Deal
2026-11-01.facts: Mark Walter is selling the Lakers to Josh Kushner in a deal that values the franchise at $12.5 billion, sources told ESPN. The transaction came together in just 72 hours of secret negotiations, with Walter and the Thrive Capital founder finalizing terms Thursday and expected to sign the formal agreement soon.

2026-11-01.title: Thunder Lose Holmgren for Two Months After Latest Injury Wave
2026-11-01.facts: Chet Holmgren will miss eight to ten weeks with a knee injury, the Thunder announced, delivering another major blow to a team already reeling from injuries. The timing couldn't be worse for Oklahoma City—Holmgren went down just days after the Thunder lost both Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace to extended absences earlier this week.

2026-11-01.title: Anthropic Blocks Claude from Video Game Reverse-Engineering
2026-11-01.facts: Anthropic just rolled out sweeping new restrictions that prevent Claude from reverse-engineering or cloning video games—and the policy is catching a lot more than just piracy attempts. The company says it's cracking down on users who try to recreate existing games by feeding Claude screenshots, code snippets, or gameplay descriptions and asking it to rebuild the mechanics or assets.

2026-11-02.title: Pope Flies Commercial on Global Tours
2026-11-02.facts: Pope Leo the Fourteenth doesn't have Air Force One. He doesn't even have a private jet.

2026-11-02.title: Cyberattack Targets Supermarket Freezers Across Europe
2026-11-02.facts: Supermarket freezers in Belgium and Sweden were hit by what authorities are calling a suspected cyberattack over the weekend. One store in Sweden reported that the temperature controls for its freezers were remotely reset to fifty degrees Celsius—that's a hundred and twenty-two degrees Fahrenheit—hot enough to spoil everything inside.

2026-11-02.title: China Tightens Grip on Critical Technology Exports
2026-11-02.facts: Beijing is making it harder for other countries to break free from their dependence on Chinese technology. It's not just rare earth minerals anymore.

2026-11-02.title: Fighting Escalates in Yemen as Coalition Intercepts Missile
2026-11-02.facts: A Saudi-led coalition intercepted a missile over the weekend as fighting intensified in Yemen's northern al-Jawf province. Houthi-affiliated media reported that seven people were wounded in airstrikes on the port city of Hodeidah, a critical gateway for humanitarian aid.

2026-11-02.title: Elon Musk's Record-Breaking Election Spending
2026-11-02.facts: Elon Musk is testing the limits of what money can buy in American politics this election cycle. The billionaire has spent nearly half a billion dollars on the midterms—a sum that eclipses anything ever spent by a single person who wasn't actually running for office.

2026-11-02.title: Judge to Hear Motion in Lindsay Clancy Murder Case
2026-11-02.facts: A Massachusetts judge will hear arguments Monday on whether to dismiss charges against Lindsay Clancy, in a hearing that could reshape one of the state's most closely watched murder cases. Clancy is facing first-degree murder charges in connection with the deaths of her children, a case that's drawn intense public scrutiny since it began.

2026-11-02.title: Senate Control Hangs in the Balance After Midterms
2026-11-02.facts: Control of the U.S. Senate after Tuesday's midterms could come down to scenarios that sound more like political fiction than reality.

2026-11-02.title: Goldman Predicts Oil Could Hit $130 a Barrel
2026-11-02.facts: Goldman Sachs is warning that oil prices could surge to an average of $130 per barrel next year if the Middle East crisis escalates. The investment bank's analysts say Brent crude could spike as high as $140 a barrel if tensions between the U.S., Israel, and Iran continue to worsen.

2026-11-02.title: Virgin Media O2 Planning Thousands of Job Cuts
2026-11-02.facts: Virgin Media O2 is preparing to cut thousands of jobs as the British broadband and mobile provider looks to slash costs. The company hasn't finalized the exact number, but the BBC reports it's likely to be a sizable chunk of the workforce.

2026-11-02.title: Deutsche Bank Calls Time to Buy Tech Again
2026-11-02.facts: Tech stocks have staged dramatic V-shaped recoveries five times in the past thirty months—and Deutsche Bank thinks we're about to see number six. The bank's analysts say investor positioning in technology has gotten so pessimistic that it no longer reflects the sector's actual earnings growth, which remains strong.

2026-11-02.title: Mortgage Rates Could Drop Below Seven Percent Soon
2026-11-02.facts: Mortgage rates below seven percent are back in play for the first time in a while. Rates have been falling lately, and the recent drop has started to breathe some life back into housing demand over the past two weeks.

2026-11-02.title: Ravens Lose Jackson for Season With Thumb Injury
2026-11-02.facts: Lamar Jackson's season is over. The Ravens quarterback needs surgery on his right thumb and will be placed on injured reserve, head coach Jesse Minter announced Sunday.

2026-11-02.title: Thunder lose Holmgren for up to ten weeks as injuries mount
2026-11-02.facts: Chet Holmgren's going to miss eight to ten weeks with a knee injury, and it couldn't have come at a worse time for Oklahoma City. The Thunder already lost Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace to extended absences earlier this week, meaning their roster depth is suddenly looking razor-thin.

2026-11-02.title: Lakers' family feud spills into public as ownership battle intensifies
2026-11-02.facts: Jeanie Buss is accusing her own siblings of working behind her back in a legal fight that's turning the Lakers' ownership dispute into a full-blown family drama. The accusation, filed in court documents, claims her brothers and sisters used what she calls "cloak and dagger" tactics as they push to sell their shares in the franchise.

2026-11-02.title: Claude Now Blocks Video Game Recreation
2026-11-02.facts: Anthropic's putting new guardrails on what Claude can build—specifically, it's now blocking attempts to recreate existing video games. The update went live this week, preventing Claude from coding up clones of commercial titles, even if users are just tinkering for educational purposes.

2026-11-03.title: US Strikes Iranian Island Ahead of Midterm Elections
2026-11-03.facts: American forces have launched strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first attack on that location since June. US officials described the operation as limited and defensive, but the timing—just hours before midterm elections—has raised questions about the strategic calculus behind the move.

2026-11-03.title: Australian Court Hears Challenge to Social Media Age Ban
2026-11-03.facts: Reddit and an Australian digital rights group are taking the government to court over a new law that bans children under 16 from using major social media platforms. The challengers argue the restriction violates constitutional rights to free expression and access to information.

2026-11-03.title: Midterm Elections Underway With Control of Senate in Question
2026-11-03.facts: Voters across the country are heading to the polls today in midterm elections that could reshape the balance of power in Washington. Republicans are bracing for potential losses amid what's being described as a backlash to the president's economic leadership and the Iran war.

2026-11-03.title: Trump Voting Fraud Crackdown Yields Just 236 Charges
2026-11-03.facts: The Trump administration's effort to prove widespread noncitizen voting has led to just 236 people being charged with voting-fraud-related offenses so far. That's a strikingly small number given the administration's repeated and unsubstantiated claims that fraud is rampant across the country.

2026-11-03.title: Trump Administration Moves to Scale Back Workplace Protections for Pregnant Workers
2026-11-03.facts: The Trump administration is preparing to roll back parts of a Biden-era law that was designed to help pregnant women stay in the workforce. The Pregnant Workers Fairness Act required employers to make accommodations for pregnancy-related conditions, but some conservatives have argued that the regulations implementing it went too far.

2026-11-03.title: Michigan Voters to Weigh In on Trump's Trade War at the Polls
2026-11-03.facts: President Trump's tariff strategy is facing a real-world test in Michigan, where voters head to the polls with trade policy squarely on their minds. The president's tariffs and his ongoing trade battles with Canada have become a central issue in the state, which has deep ties to both manufacturing and cross-border commerce.

2026-11-03.title: UK and EU Reach Deal to Cut Post-Brexit Food Export Red Tape
2026-11-03.facts: Britain and the European Union have agreed to a draft deal that would eliminate a significant chunk of the bureaucratic burden that's been choking food exports since Brexit. The agreement is the most substantial piece of the so-called Brexit reset that the two sides have managed to finalize so far.

2026-11-03.title: Nasdaq-100 Slides Into Third Correction of the Year
2026-11-03.facts: The Nasdaq-100 has tumbled into its third correction of 2025, and this time it's artificial intelligence worries driving the selloff. The tech-heavy index dropped enough to meet the technical definition of a correction—a decline of at least ten percent from recent highs.

2026-11-03.title: Los Angeles Faces $20 Million Fine Over Blocked Housing Project
2026-11-03.facts: A developer is seeking twenty million dollars in damages from the City of Los Angeles, claiming officials illegally delayed approval of a new housing project. The developer's legal team says the city's denial violates both AB 2011 and the Housing Accountability Act—state laws designed to speed up housing construction in California.

2026-11-03.title: Spanish Soccer Player Dies After On-Field Collision
2026-11-03.facts: Jesús de Miguel has died at age 30 following an on-field collision during a match on Monday. The Tenerife forward collapsed after the incident during a Spanish second-division game, and his club confirmed his death Tuesday.

2026-11-03.title: Thunder to Retire Westbrook's Number Zero
2026-11-03.facts: The Oklahoma City Thunder are bringing Russell Westbrook's number zero back home permanently. The franchise announced it'll retire his jersey later this season, honoring the former MVP who spent the first eleven years of his career in Oklahoma City.

2026-11-03.title: Gilgeous-Alexander Drops Forty-Three to Hand Cavs First Home Loss
2026-11-03.facts: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had what his teammates are calling "the look" Monday night, and Cleveland found out what that means the hard way. He poured in a season-high forty-three points, including a go-ahead three-pointer with just over thirty seconds left, as Oklahoma City handed the Cavaliers their first home loss of the season, 117-112.

2026-11-04.title: World Leaders Grapple With Trump's Midterm Losses
2026-11-04.facts: World leaders and commentators are trying to decode what President Trump's electoral losses in the midterms will mean for their countries. The administration's foreign policy faces new constraints now that Democrats have taken Congress, and that's raising questions from Tehran to Caracas.

2026-11-04.title: Democrats Flip South Carolina Senate Seat in Historic Upset
2026-11-04.facts: Annie Andrews has defeated Darline Graham in South Carolina's Senate race, becoming the state's first Democratic senator in almost three decades. Graham had been handpicked by President Trump to fill the seat after her brother's death, making the loss particularly stinging for the White House.

2026-11-04.title: Delhi Chokes on Toxic Air as Diwali Approaches
2026-11-04.facts: Delhi's air has turned toxic again, with the city's air quality index hitting 377 on Wednesday morning—a reading that puts it in the "very poor" category. The timing couldn't be worse, as Diwali celebrations are just around the corner and firework restrictions have now entered force.

2026-11-04.title: Houthi Blockade Traps Yemenis in Taiz
2026-11-04.facts: A monthlong siege by Houthi forces on the Yemeni city of Taiz is creating what aid groups are calling a looming catastrophe. The blockade has cut off food, water, fuel, and medical supplies to the trapped population, leaving residents in increasingly desperate conditions.

2026-11-04.title: Democrats Seize Congress in Historic Midterm Sweep
2026-11-04.facts: Democrats have taken control of Congress for the remainder of Donald Trump's presidency, pulling off wins in races that weren't supposed to be close. Two Senate contests that looked like toss-ups a year ago turned into comfortable Democratic victories, part of a night that saw the party push deep into traditionally Republican territory.

2026-11-04.title: England Trials Multi-Cancer Blood Test in Primary Care
2026-11-04.facts: A blood test that can detect multiple types of cancer at once is coming to some GP surgeries in England, marking a significant shift in how hard-to-diagnose cancers might be caught. The test is designed to identify abdominal cancers—including liver, ovarian, and pancreatic cancer—that are notoriously difficult to diagnose in their early stages.

2026-11-04.title: Americans Cast Ballots from Space Station and Antarctica
2026-11-04.facts: Astronauts aboard the International Space Station joined Americans in Antarctica and remote Alaskan villages in casting absentee ballots in the midterm elections, demonstrating just how far the reach of U.S. voting extends.

2026-11-04.title: Trump Administration Targets Pregnancy Workplace Protections
2026-11-04.facts: The Trump administration is preparing to roll back workplace protections for pregnant workers that were only recently put in place. The move would scale back a Biden-era law designed to help women stay in their jobs during pregnancy.

2026-11-04.title: Canva Slashes Workforce After Toughest Year on Record
2026-11-04.facts: Canva is cutting more than a thousand jobs in what CEO Melanie Perkins is calling the company's hardest year yet. The Australian design software giant says some employees will lose their jobs outright, while others will be asked to switch roles as the company restructures.

2026-11-04.title: Super Micro Delivers Earnings Beat on AI Server Boom
2026-11-04.facts: Super Micro's stock surged Wednesday after the company's latest earnings report showed just how much money there is to be made building the infrastructure behind artificial intelligence. The chip and server maker posted results that blew past Wall Street's expectations, driven by what CFO Mark Long called a "high-quality customer base" that's snapping up AI servers as fast as the company can build them.

2026-11-04.title: Mortgage Servicing Rights Hit Highest Valuations in Decades
2026-11-04.facts: Mortgage servicing rights are trading at their richest levels in more than twenty years, and lenders are splitting into two very different camps on what to do about it. The financial instruments that represent the right to service a loan—collecting payments, managing escrow, handling defaults—have become suddenly valuable as interest rates stay elevated and refinancing activity stays low.

2026-11-04.title: Spanish Police Investigate Player's Death After On-Field Collision
2026-11-04.facts: Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel has died at age 30 following an on-field collision during a Spanish second-division match on Monday, and now police have opened an investigation into the incident. The collision happened during a LaLiga 2 game, and de Miguel's club confirmed his death shortly after.

2026-11-04.title: Dumont Family Takes Control of Mavericks
2026-11-04.facts: Sivan and Patrick Dumont are now running the Dallas Mavericks after purchasing Miriam Adelson's shares last month, giving the Dumont family nearly 70 percent of the franchise. It's a major ownership shift for one of the NBA's marquee teams.

2026-11-04.title: Message Threads Cut Claude Code Latency Without Hiking Your Bill
2026-11-04.facts: Anthropic just shipped a performance upgrade to Claude Code that'll change how you structure long-running tasks—and it's one of those rare optimizations where you get speed without paying for it. The new message threads feature lets Claude Code maintain context across multiple back-and-forth exchanges within a single session, but here's the non-obvious win: because threads reuse the same context window instead of re-sending the full conversation history with every turn, you're cutting latency by up to 40% on multi-step workflows without inflating your token count.
